There's so much greatness in Sea of Thieves to enjoy that could be polished further and expanded upon, but the game is severely held back by bugs, crashes and hilariously bad sword- and gunplay for its PvP element.

In a pirate game I expect to face off against other players in epic duels, perhaps with some role playing element on top as the cherry. But nope, combat on the ships pretty much consists of people throwing their bodies at your vessel to try and lower your anchor, whilst bunny hopping around and abusing mechanics like the sweatiest cocaine addict the world has ever seen. Oh, and don't get me started on the bloodthirsty, arrogant players who will literally chase you across the world to fight you. Did I also mention they will spawn camp you and shout slurs as well?

I wish the game had a bigger emphasis on the naval combat and significantly more realistic duelling. Having people throw themselves at your ship again and again is just laughable gameplay. There could be so much more depth here, like adding booby traps and allowing us to protect our anchor and ladders, but I'm afraid the devs don't care.

The game that really brought my friends together during 2020. Sea of Thieves offers quite a bit! Quests and puzzles to solve, dangers to contend with, rival players to keep you on your toes, epic storylines unfolding across the years. One of the best parts is a deep sense of accomplishment when you fought tooth and nail to earn it, especially special/world events. Despite the many bugs and issues, this is a game that's constantly evolving. And for the most part? It's for the better! Safe travels and much treasure, and I'll see you on the high seas!

Such a massive game install (130gb) for nothing but shiny water graphics and no substance. Every time I've ever reinstalled this game I am met with nothing but the reminder of a game that we conceptualize in our minds to be fun but is nothing more than a fetch quest missing any actual gameplay. 80% of this game is just micro-managing a boat to the destination. The other 20% is doing the quick looting on usually a small island, sometimes a big island, then rinse and repeat.

Even in games like GTA Online the heist prep/setup missions are more engaging, traveling from Point A to Point B isn't padded with long trips via a singular boat across long stretches of water.

The sea has basically become my escape from reality at this point. This and a full band of friends playing different instruments while listening to the sounds of the waves have helped me relax from my hectic student life.

This is a good game. By no means is it perfect or my favorite, but it gets the important things right and keeps you interested and engaged.

Buying this game started as a joke between me and my pals. We are never one to grind for anything that much but we still bought it. After a few days of playing it, my friends being more inclined towards FPS types of games and DOTA 2 felt that SOT requires a different kind of learning curve than most games we play together and started to think that it just isn't for them. Needless to say, after sinking a few times to sweaty pirates, my friends called it a bust and deleted the game. I on the other hand loved it. It is difficult but I love the fact that it is an open-world (or sea) game and that it offers something new to the table every time I boot it up, my only problem was finding people to play. Good thing then that SOT has a very much alive community and there are tons of servers in Discord that help one who is new to this game find new friends with whom they can sail with! After a few months of playing the game almost everyday, I found additional people I now include in my circle of friends, even my wife plays it with me now as well! Sea of Thieves is one of my most favorite games I played this 2023 and it is not even mid year yet! Honestly, it is one of my favorite games I've ever played!
